title: Redwood security review - SSO/SCIM + RBAC
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Greenleaf Health's security team through SSO (SAML) and SCIM provisioning options and discussed RBAC/least-privilege mapping. Key topics: SAML IdP metadata, Just-in-Time vs SCIM provisioning, SCIM attribute mapping, group-to-role mapping in Redwood, audit logs and retention, KMS & encryption at rest, SOC 2 implications, and private deployment options for data residency. Agreed next steps: share implementation docs, sample SAML metadata, SCIM mapping spreadsheet, and schedule test SSO connection in staging next week.
topics: SAML SSO setup and metadata exchange
RBAC role mapping and least-privilege model
Data residency and private deployment options
transcript:
[00:00] Mia Carter (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Lina Morales (CISO): Lina here. Rahul and Sofia are with me.
[00:09] Rahul Singh (IT Admin): Rahul, hi.
[00:11] Sofia Alvarez (Security Engineer): Sofia here.
[00:14] Daniel Park (SE): Daniel from Redwood, thanks for having us.
[00:17] Mia Carter (AE): We'll run through SSO, SCIM and how RBAC looks in Redwood. We booked 45, so we'll keep it focused.
[00:28] Lina: Great, high level context: we're evaluating vendors for customer-facing features, data is PHI-adjacent, so we need SOC 2 plus strong least-privilege access, SSO with our IdP and SCIM provisioning for accounts. Also, data residency — EU region preference.
[00:42] Daniel: Understood. Quick note: Redwood supports SAML 2.0, SP-initiated and IdP-initiated, plus SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. We also have Just-In-Time provisioning toggle if you want less churn.
[00:55] Sofia: When you say toggle, is that JIT only creating local accounts on first login vs full SCIM sync?
[01:01] Daniel: Exactly. JIT creates accounts on first sign-in and you can map groups, but SCIM gives full lifecycle: create, update, deactivate. SCIM is recommended for enterprise-managed lifecycle.
[01:10] Rahul: Our IdP is Okta, but we also have one team on Azure AD. Do you support both?
[01:15] Daniel: Yes, both. We often see Okta and Azure AD. We'll share sample metadata for each.
[01:21] Mia: Quick security point — you mentioned SOC 2, Lina — we can share our SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA, plus our ISO attestation if needed.
[01:30] Lina: Yes please, we'll need SOC 2. Also want to confirm audit logging granularity — who did what, when, include token-level usage?
[01:39] Daniel: Our audit logs capture admin actions (user create/deactivate, role changes, API key events), plus per-request traces with request id. Token-level usage breakdown is in Console under usage logs, not per-token content but metadata — caller, model, tokens.
[01:52] Sofia: Retention period? We have to meet 12 months for internal audit.
[01:56] Daniel: Default retention is 90 days; enterprise plans can extend to configurable retention windows — we have options for 12 months or longer as an add-on. We'll include retention SLAs in the contract.
[02:08] Rahul: For SCIM mapping: we map Okta groups to internal roles. How do you handle group-to-role mapping?
[02:14] Daniel: Redwood allows mapping SCIM group names to predefined roles (admin, developer, viewer) or custom roles. You can apply scope restrictions — e.g., project-level roles. We will show the mapping UI during the test.
[02:26] Mia: Also note we support attribute-based access control patterns via group attributes; you can provision a group per environment (prod/staging) and map accordingly.
[02:35] Lina: On the encryption/KMS side — does Redwood use customer-managed keys or only provider-managed?
[02:41] Daniel: For hosted customers we offer provider-managed encryption by default. For enterprise/private deployments we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM-backed options for Private. We'll share the KMS integration guide.
[02:55] Sofia: Do keys encrypt data at rest only or also in use?
[02:59] Daniel: Primarily at rest and disk-level encryption; for in-use we rely on secure enclaves and runtime protections. For full control you can deploy Private and control the key material in your VPC.
[03:12] Rahul: Data residency: we need EU-only storage. Is that supported for hosted?
[03:17] Daniel: Yes, we have EU regions; for strict residency customers we recommend Private deployment or a dedicated region contract to guarantee data doesn't leave region.
[03:25] Lina: Ok, let's get into RBAC specifics — least-privilege. We want separation between model operators and app developers.
[03:31] Daniel: Typical pattern: create granular roles — e.g., Model-Runner (can invoke models but not manage keys), Model-Admin (can configure models, rollouts), and Security-Admin (audit and org-level settings). Roles are additive and you can scope to projects.
[03:44] Sofia: Can we restrict a role to only a subset of models or to production vs staging?
[03:49] Daniel: Yes, scoping is supported. You can pin roles to model tags or specific model ids, and environment scoping is possible with project-level bindings.
[03:58] Rahul: How is MFA enforced for console access?
[04:02] Mia: We support SSO-enforced MFA via IdP, and we can require MFA for local accounts. Enterprise default is SSO with enforced MFA at the IdP level.
[04:12] Lina: Audit trail of role changes needs to include who changed mapping and an export for auditors.
[04:17] Daniel: Audit logs include admin id, timestamp, and diff of changes where possible. Exports are available as CSV/JSON for the retention window.
[04:28] Mia: A few common gotchas: SCIM requires the user email to match Okta/Azure unique id, and group names must match mapping rules; sometimes customers have nested groups which need flattening.
[04:41] Rahul: We have nested groups. Can SCIM handle nested group flattening?
[04:45] Daniel: SCIM spec doesn't require nested groups, but our connector can interpret nested groups by flattening if you enable that option in the SCIM configuration. We'll provide the mapping guide.
[04:58] Lina: We also have a requirement for just-in-time provisioning for contractors — they shouldn't be in the directory permanently. How do deprovisioning flows look?
[05:05] Daniel: Best practice is SCIM-based full lifecycle; on deactivate we can mark user as deactivated immediately. For JIT you need to complement with a periodic sync or a short login TTL.
[05:16] Sofia: Any known limitations with Azure AD SCIM SCIM sometimes returns different group identifier formats and we've seen mapping mismatch.
[05:24] Daniel: We have customer notes for Azure AD quirks; we'll include a troubleshooting section.
[05:30] Mia: Quick question from our side — do you need API keys to test SSO in staging?
[05:34] Rahul: Sorry, I meant, do we need a test org?
[05:36] Daniel: We'll provide a sandbox/staging org and temporary admin accounts to test SSO/SCIM. We'll coordinate on timing.
[05:44] Lina: Encryption again — for audit we need to know KMS key rotation policy and whether Redwood rotates keys or if we control rotation.
[05:51] Daniel: For provider-managed keys we rotate per provider policy; for customer-managed KMS you control rotation. We log key rotation events in the audit log.
[06:01] Sofia: SOC 2 controls mapping — do you map to specific CC controls in your artifact?
[06:06] Mia: Yes, our SOC 2 report typically includes control descriptions and mapping; we can provide a control matrix on request under NDA.
[06:14] Lina: Good. About SAML metadata exchange — what's the easiest flow with Okta?
[06:19] Daniel: We provide service provider (SP) metadata XML. In Okta you add a SAML app, import metadata, set attributes (nameID = email), and configure assertion consumer URL. We'll send step-by-step.
[06:30] Rahul: Attribute mapping — we use custom attribute 'employeeType' and groups for contractor vs employee. Can Redwood map based on custom attributes?
[06:37] Daniel: Yes, SCIM attributes and SAML attributes can be used in mapping rules. We can map employeeType to roles or tag accounts.
[06:45] Sofia: About RBAC least-privilege: can we have temporary elevation (just-in-time admin) for incident response?
[06:51] Daniel: We have time-limited role grants with expiration tokens for elevated access, integrated with SCIM deprovisioning or via manual grant from the Console. There is also ability to issue temporary API keys scoped to a role for X hours.
[07:05] Lina: Good. Are the temporary grants logged and reversible?
[07:09] Daniel: Yes, they appear in audit logs with grant/expiry timestamps.
[07:14] Mia: Quick pause — any blockers on your side for a test?
[07:17] Rahul: We need SSO docs, SCIM mapping spreadsheet, and a sandbox account. Timeline: we'd like to test next week and aim for pilot in late Oct.
[07:27] Mia: Sounds doable. We'll send docs today, set up sandbox, and propose a time slot for the test connection.
[07:34] Lina: On contracts: we may need a DPA and mention of EU data residency.
[07:39] Mia: We'll include DPA language and data residency options in the proposal.
[07:43] Sofia: One more: Where are audit logs stored — separate from customer data, and are they encrypted?
[07:49] Daniel: Audit logs are stored in our logging service, encrypted at rest; for enterprise we can stream logs to your account (e.g., S3/GCS) for retention and isolation.
[08:00] Rahul: Streaming is preferred for our auditors.
[08:03] Daniel: Noted, we have a streaming integration for logs and metrics. We'll include sample terraform.
[08:10] Lina: Is there any scenario where Redwood needs access to raw request payloads for debugging?
[08:15] Daniel: For hosted support we can request request-level logs — by default we don't expose content to Redwood engineers; support access is controlled via audited processes and requires customer approval or redaction. For PII/PHI we recommend Private or dedicated.
[08:31] Mia: Okay, let's recap next steps.
[08:33] Daniel: Quick clarifying question, do you want us to enable JIT first or go full SCIM?
[08:38] Lina: Full SCIM for employees, JIT for contractors if that's possible.
[08:43] Daniel: Good, we'll prepare SCIM mapping examples and JIT notes.
[08:47] Mia: We'll also attach SOC 2 and SAML/SCIM implementation guides.
[08:51] Rahul: Timeline — sandbox next week, pilot late Oct.
[08:55] Mia: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[08:58] Lina: Thank you.
[09:00] Sofia: Thanks.
[09:02] End of recording.
